consequences: Chunk ids reveal nothing in encrypted repositories. Prune can repack by copying sealed bytes without decrypting. The format is Keepr's own (src-tauri/engine/src/lib.rs documents the layout).
context: Backups need de-duplication across versions and files, compression, optional encryption, and must work on SMB shares where millions of small files are slow.
decision: Files are split with FastCDC (256 KiB min, 1 MiB average, 4 MiB max), each chunk named by a keyed BLAKE3 hash, zstd-compressed when that helps, sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305 when the repository is encrypted, and packed about 16 MiB to a pack file. A master key is sealed twice in keepr-repo.json, by an Argon2id key from the password and by a recovery key, so the password can change without rewriting data.
title: Content-defined chunks in packs, sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305

consequences: An interrupted backup leaves only orphan packs, which prune deletes; nothing half-done is ever a snapshot.
context: A backup can stop at any moment (sleep, a share dropping, a crash).
decision: Packs are written first, then an index file naming them, and the snapshot file last. Prune writes new packs and a new index before deleting old index files and packs. Every file is written to a temporary name and renamed.
title: Write order: packs, then index, then snapshot

consequences: A plan's encryption, retention and pruning never affect another plan. Two plans backing up the same files store them twice.
context: Plans choose encryption separately, and one destination (a NAS share) holds many plans.
decision: Each plan has its own repository in a folder of its destination. De-duplication is within a plan, not across plans.
title: One repository per plan, inside the destination

consequences: Failures show as failures in Activity and notifications; a stale-backup warning covers anything that stops running.
context: Earlier backup scripts on this Mac failed silently more than once: a vanished cloud sync root made rsync write to local disk and report success, and an evicted script exited 126 unnoticed for weeks.
decision: A source that can't be read fails the whole backup rather than being snapshotted as empty. A plan that has backed up before never creates a new repository by itself when its keepr-repo.json is missing. Cloud-only (dataless) files are skipped by default rather than downloaded.
title: A missing source or backup fails loudly

consequences: Needs Full Disk Access to mount the snapshot. Tests must not make snapshots of the Mac (Core.still_copies is off in tests). Folder nodes now carry their total size and file count so a kept folder costs nothing.
context: Files saved during a backup could be caught half old, half new; and statting a million files every hour is slow.
decision: Before a backup of folders on the Data volume, Keepr takes a local snapshot (tmutil localsnapshot), mounts it read-only and hidden, reads from it, and deletes it afterwards (and any left behind at the next launch). It notes the FSEvents id just before, and the next backup replays events since then: folders macOS says didn't change are taken whole from the previous snapshot. Dropped or wrapped events, or a different parent, mean looking at everything; weekly full backups re-read everything.
title: Read the startup disk through an APFS snapshot, and trust FSEvents for unchanged folders

consequences: One Keychain prompt per new build instead of one per secret, and none within a run. A Developer ID with a Team ID would remove the per-build prompt entirely.
context: A self-signed app has no Team ID, so the Keychain's partition list for its items names each build's code hash; after every rebuild macOS asks again for every item, whatever Always Allow said. With three items (plan password, recovery key, SMB password) that was three prompts per build.
decision: Keepr keeps all its secrets as a JSON map in one generic-password item (service Keepr, account secrets), reads it once per run and keeps it in memory; older one-per-secret items are moved in on first use and deleted.
title: All secrets in one Keychain item, cached for the run

consequences: Snapshot ids change, so the next backup doesn't trust FSEvents and looks at everything once. The removal runs as a job with progress and Stop.
context: Taking a folder out of a plan left its versions in every old snapshot, with no way to reclaim the space.
decision: Removing a source from a plan that has backed up asks: keep its versions, or delete its backed-up data (confirmed a second time). Deleting rewrites every snapshot without that source (new snapshots written before the old ones are removed), then reclaims packs as prune does.
title: Removing a source can delete its backed-up data

consequences: Plans that don't skip cloud-only files download them and they stay downloaded. Cloud-folder destinations can be read after the service frees up space.
context: Apps launched by launchd start with IOPOL_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES off, so reading a cloud-only File Provider file or listing a dataless folder fails with EDEADLK, but only when unattended. Seen before in backup-manager.
decision: Call setiopolicy_np(IOPOL_TYPE_VFS_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES, process, ON) at the top of cli(), before the app or any command starts. Cloud-folder sources are read live, never through the APFS still copy, because a read-only snapshot cannot materialise.
title: Keepr turns on dataless-file materialisation for its own process

consequences: Anyone passing on Keepr, changed or not, must do so under the GPL with its source.
context: The owner plans to make the repository public and wants the app to stay free, as Two-edged Sword is. Every dependency's licence (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, OFL for JetBrains Mono) is compatible.
decision: LICENSE is the GNU GPL v3 text; package.json, Cargo.toml and the engine's Cargo.toml say GPL-3.0-or-later; the bundle's copyright line (the About box) names it; Settings shows it under the version; features.md › Licence and credits (a Help page) and the README's Licence section explain it.
title: Keepr is GPL-3.0-or-later

consequences: Existing plans pick up the attribute rule (serde default yes) but not the new default rules. A folder kept unchanged by FSEvents isn't re-checked, so an item marked after it was backed up stays until the next full backup
context: Time Machine skips items apps tag with the com_apple_backup_excludeItem attribute (caches, re-downloadable data), and its fixed list of system exclusions is no longer a readable file on current macOS
decision: A plan setting, on by default, leaves out anything carrying the attribute; new plans also exclude the per-drive macOS folders (.Spotlight-V100, .fseventsd, .Trashes, .DocumentRevisions-V100, .TemporaryItems)
title: Keepr skips what apps mark for backups to skip

consequences: make fmt before committing; a new source file without the header fails make lint
context: The code had no formatter or linter; lines run wide by design
decision: rustfmt and Prettier at 140 columns, Clippy with warnings as errors, ESLint with typescript-eslint and react-hooks recommended but react-hooks/set-state-in-effect off, since resetting a page's own state in an effect is used deliberately; make check runs make lint, and tools/license_headers.py keeps the GPL header on every source file
title: Lint and format with rustfmt, Clippy, Prettier and ESLint

consequences: A repository settles at a few small packs rather than hundreds. A merged pack under 4 MB is merged again next time, so a few MB are rewritten per tidy-up until it grows past the threshold. Like any rewrite, a cloud folder may sync the deletions before the new pack uploads.
context: Every backup ends with a pack of whatever was left over, often a few KB. With hourly backups to a cloud-synced folder (OneDrive) that is dozens of tiny files a day, each synced on its own.
decision: reclaim() copies packs under a quarter of PACK_TARGET (4 MB) into fuller ones once there are at least 8, through the same write-new, index, then delete path as thin-pack rewrites.
title: The daily tidy-up merges small packs

consequences: Many local builds share one version until it's released; an explicit VERSION= still sets it
context: make app bumped the patch number on every build, so local installs used up numbers that were never released
decision: bump_version.py keeps the current version unless v<version> is tagged on origin (local tags if origin can't be reached)
title: The version only bumps past a released one

consequences: Listing a folder in the newest snapshot stats its entries and reads the folder on disk; items only on the Mac can't be ticked, opened or removed
context: Deletions and new files only showed after the next backup, which read as Keepr being wrong
decision: For the newest snapshot of a folder source, entries missing on disk show Not on Mac, and items on disk but not in the snapshot show Not backed up, filtered through the plan's own rules (engine backup::Rules) so left-out files never show
title: Restore marks the newest snapshot against the Mac now

consequences: The command's own result never changes the backup's; it can't stop the backup (a Stop doesn't kill it) and is cut off after 2 minutes; a repeat of waiting for the same missing destination doesn't run it again
context: Home Assistant was told of backup failures by the old backup scripts, which Keepr replaced
decision: Each plan has an After each backup command, run whatever the result with the outcome in KEEPR_* variables (KEEPR_PLAN_IDS lists every enabled plan); nothing Home Assistant-specific is built into Keepr, and the reporter script lives in the ha-config repo
title: Plans report outcomes through an after-backup command

consequences: All 26 docs images in about 50 seconds with nothing on screen. The window chrome is drawn, not captured: if macOS changes its buttons, chrome() needs new measurements. Screenshots are macOS only.
context: Retaking the docs screenshots flashed app windows on screen one at a time and needed Screen Recording permission; Brainstead had already solved this.
decision: Ported from Brainstead: in screenshot mode (KEEPR_SCENE) the window is fully transparent, click-through, out of the Dock and never takes focus, and the app saves WKWebView's takeSnapshot to KEEPR_SNAPSHOT after KEEPR_SNAPSHOT_AFTER seconds. tools/screenshots.py draws the unfocused window buttons and rounded corners back on, retries a blank shot from a fresh launch, and runs 4 apps at once (-j), each with its own copy of the demo app data. The splash's fade-in is switched off in screenshot mode, as the invisible window can hold it at its first, empty frame. window_id.swift is gone.
title: Screenshots are taken unseen, from the webview's snapshot

consequences: A new screen needs a topic (help.test.ts fails otherwise, run by make check through vitest). A changed screen updates its src/help topic as well as its docs/ guide. Keyboard shortcuts in the drawer come from src/help/keyboard.md. Two copies of user-facing text now exist: the drawer's short topics and docs/'s full guides.
context: The user wanted in-app help like Brainstead's: help for the screen you're on, searchable, with getting-started guides. Keepr already had an Apple Help Book built from docs/ on ⌘?.
decision: Topics are src/help/*.md (frontmatter plus ## sections; guides' sections are steps), imported raw by src/help/index.ts and shown by src/help/HelpDrawer.tsx on the right under the toolbar. ? (outside a text box), the toolbar's ? button and Help › Keepr Help (⌘?, which now emits 'help' to the window) open it on the current screen's topic. app: links open screens (app:plans/new, app:destinations/add), help: links other topics. Finished guides are ticked in the webview's localStorage only. The Help Book moves to Help › Keepr User Guide and the drawer's footer button.
title: In-app help is a drawer of markdown topics; the Help Book stays as the user guide

consequences: A changed feature updates its docs/ guide and its src/help topic in the same change. pandoc and hiutil are no longer build needs. macOS's Help menu search finds menu items only, not help text; the drawer's own search covers the topics.
context: With the help drawer added, the same user text lived in src/help topics and in the Help Book built from docs/, and the two would drift. The user chose to drop the Help Book, as Brainstead did.
decision: Help › Keepr Help (⌘?), ? and the toolbar's ? button open the drawer of src/help/*.md topics; there is no other in-app help. tools/helpbook.py, the bundled Keepr.help, its Info.plist keys, make help and the helpd cache clearing in make install-app are removed. docs/ stays as the user guides on GitHub.
title: In-app help is the drawer alone; the Help Book is gone

consequences: make screenshots refreshes the website too, with no extra step. Pages serves nothing until the Actions source is chosen in repository settings. Anyone previewing locally needs a server that follows symlinks (python3 -m http.server does).
context: Wayne wanted an Apple-style product page in plain HTML, CSS and JS for GitHub Pages, using the docs' screenshots. Pages' branch mode runs Jekyll in safe mode, which ignores symlinks, and copying the PNGs into site/ would duplicate 1 MB that make screenshots regenerates.
decision: site/index.html, style.css and main.js are the page; site/images is a symlink to ../docs/images so a local static server shows the current screenshots. .github/workflows/pages.yml copies site/ and docs/images/*.png into one artifact and deploys it, so Pages must be set to the GitHub Actions source. The page uses only the light theme; deep links (#plan, #restore, …) are the tour's steps.
title: Product page lives in site/, deployed to GitHub Pages by Actions

consequences: After make screenshots, re-run cwebp on the screens the page uses (overview, plan, restore, versions, search, sizemap, menu-bar) or the page falls behind the docs. The site has no dependency on docs/images at publish time.
context: D-20261008-01 had site/images as a symlink to docs/images and a workflow that copied the PNGs in. Publishing the way Brainstead did asks for WebP (cwebp -q 80), an OG card, a touch icon and a Pages workflow that uploads site/ as it is.
decision: site/img holds WebP copies of the light screenshots it uses (about 300 KB in all, from 1.3 MB of PNG), plus og.png (1200x630, rendered from an HTML card with headless Chrome) and icon-180.png. .github/workflows/pages.yml uploads site/ unchanged. Supersedes D-20261008-01's symlink and copy step.
title: The product page keeps its own WebP screenshots in site/img

consequences: Rows must stay one fixed height (ROW in Restore.tsx matches .file-row); a reveal scrolls by row index, not scrollIntoView, since the row may not be drawn.
context: A backed-up folder with thousands of files drew every row at once and re-sorted the tree on every render, freezing the Restore screen.
decision: Draw only the rows in view (fixed 32px rows, spacers above and below), and memoise the sorted tree of rows. Chosen over Disk Usage Visualiser's scroll-to-load paging because the list is a tree with folders opening in place, and Show in Files must jump to a row deep in it.
title: Restore file list is windowed, not paged

consequences: Jobs that write state need the exclusive data-folder lock, so they refuse while the app runs; read-only commands use a frozen Core and run beside it. make install-cli links the binary into a bin folder on PATH.
context: The CLI was six --flags on the app binary with no help, ids only, no machine output, and an unknown flag silently opened the app.
decision: Subcommands via clap (help per command, --version, completions), plans named by id or name, --json for results on stdout with progress and errors on stderr, exit codes 0/1/2/3/130, Ctrl-C stops a job at a safe point, --yes for remove-path. Any argument means the CLI; none (or -psn_) opens the app. Old flags are mapped to their commands with a deprecation note.
title: The command line is keepr <command>, built on clap

consequences: A job queued during the few seconds of install and restart is dropped; scheduled ones are queued again after the restart. Anything added to Quit belongs in quitting.
context: AppHandle::restart ends the process at once; a backup or restore running then would be cut short, and the queue isn't saved.
decision: Install refuses while a job runs or is queued, downloads first, then Core::hold stops jobs starting (under the queue's lock, so none slips in after the check) until the restart; a failed install releases it. The restart does what Quit does first (lib.rs quitting).
title: An update's restart holds the job queue

consequences: Totals match the Space used card exactly. A copy of a file adds nothing; a deleted folder still shows while its versions are kept; if the snapshot that first stored data is pruned, the data moves to the next one that has it, which can make it look newly stored. The first map of a plan reads every listing in its history.
context: The Size Map's second map shares out a plan's stored space (after de-duplication and compression) among folders, and it must add up to the Space used card, which is the sum of every blob in the index. A chunk shared by several files or versions can only be counted once.
decision: Walk snapshots oldest first and count each chunk in the folder of the first file that references it, each listing (tree blob) once in a Folder listings block, and every index blob no snapshot reaches in a Not used by any snapshot block. Growth is what snapshots since the week before stored. The result is cached per plan until its snapshots or index change.
title: The stored map counts each piece of data once, where it was first stored

consequences: Advice quality rests on folder names and the per-folder facts; a run's Ask button adds its message and log tail, which can name a file. Anything outside the allowed keys is refused, so destinations, sources and encryption stay manual.
context: Ask (Tidemark's assistant, ported) runs an AI CLI signed in on the Mac. Backups hold work files whose names can be confidential, and a wrong exclude silently stops a file being backed up.
decision: The context names plans and folders with sizes, growth, stored space, file-type mix by size, recency and .gitignore status, plus repeated folder-name totals and recent runs; it never names files or sends contents, and a plan can be left out (then only its name goes). The AI proposes changes as a keepr-change JSON block limited to excludes, gitignore/cloud-only/marked/size-limit switches, retention and schedule; Keepr checks it (diff, what the latest backup would lose, snapshots a tidy-up would remove, warnings) and applies it only on Apply through save_plan_now, recording a change run with Undo.
title: Ask sends Keepr's figures and folder names, never files, and changes plans only through checked proposals

consequences: New slow commands should take a token and call cancel::check in their loops. Engine-internal loops (search_all, versions) aren't interruptible mid-way; search everywhere stops between plans and reads plans in parallel.
context: On a remote destination (S3, SMB, a synced cloud folder) browsing re-read every snapshot file per request and nothing could be stopped, so leaving a screen left network reads running.
decision: Repo::snapshots keeps snapshots by file name (their files are immutable), and Core trusts a repository seen in the last 30 s except for a backup. Slow browse commands take an optional token; cancel.rs runs them under a Control the window can cancel (Stop, a newer request in the same slot, or leaving the screen via useRequests), checked as listings are read and handed to restore for Quick Look copies. A stopped request answers 'Stopped.', which the window doesn't show.
title: Browse requests carry a cancel token; the snapshot list is cached by file name

consequences: Stacked changes undo independently. A change whose settings the user edited since can't be undone; they change it in the plan instead.
context: Undo used to save the whole plan as it was, so undoing an Ask change also reverted every later edit (sources added, Leave out of Ask, a newer Ask change).
decision: ask-changes/<id>.json holds the rules added/removed and each touched setting (retention and schedule per field) with before and after values. Undo refuses if a touched setting no longer has the change's after value; rules are removed/re-added without refusing. Files in the old whole-plan form are refused and deleted.
title: Ask's undo puts back only the fields its change touched

consequences: A new setup step needs a step() call with the right n and total. Setups that send no steps (listing buckets) still get the spinner.
context: R2 setup looked stuck: making the bucket and token, then waiting up to 90s for the new key to work, showed only a static line.
decision: Each API-driven setup (AWS CLI, B2, R2, CloudShell paste) takes a step callback (cloud_setup::Step: n, of, text); lib.rs emits it as setup-step events, and SetupBusy in KeySetup.tsx shows a spinner, the step's words, Step n of m and a bar. The key-wait in aws_setup::finish reports elapsed seconds.
title: Destination setup reports its steps to the setup card

consequences: Nothing backs up from the new Mac until the user checks the folders and turns the plan on, so no snapshot is added with missing sources. Restore works at once. A share source comes back as a plain folder path and needs re-adding as a share.
context: Open an existing backup lets a new Mac (or one whose plan was deleted) restore from a Keepr backup already at a destination. The backup's folders come from its newest snapshot, as absolute paths that may not exist on this Mac.
decision: Core::open_backup makes a plan pointing at the existing folder, marked created, with the newest snapshot's local paths as its sources and enabled false. Bucket sources (s3://) are left out, since their keys aren't in the backup. The name comes from the folder, without its 6-character id.
title: An opened existing backup becomes a plan that starts turned off

consequences: Big folders take longer to look through on Windows, and a file replaced by one with the same size and both times would be missed until the weekly full backup. Files changing mid-backup are read as they are. A later port of VSS or the change journal would replace the stand-ins in other.rs.
context: macOS gives Keepr an APFS snapshot of the startup disk for each backup (still.rs) and FSEvents' record of which folders changed (fsevents.rs). Windows' equivalents, Volume Shadow Copy and the NTFS change journal, need an administrator, and Keepr runs as the user. std gives no file index on Windows without a handle per file.
decision: On Windows other.rs gives still and fsevents stand-ins that say there's nothing, so every backup walks every folder and compares each file with the last snapshot. A file is unchanged when its size, modified time and creation time (standing in for macOS's status-change time) match; the inode is 0. A file's mode is read-only or not. Cloud-only files are told by their attributes (recall on open or on data access, offline). Time Machine's skip mark has no Windows counterpart, so its switch is hidden there.
title: Windows has no still copy and no change record; files count as unchanged by size and times

consequences: Secrets show in Control Panel > Credential Manager > Windows Credentials. A process with no logon session (started over SSH, or as a service) can't read or save them, so an encrypted plan or a share with a saved password fails there; the app at sign-in has one. Its test skips without a session.
context: macOS keeps all of Keepr's secrets in one Keychain item because every rebuild of a self-signed app is asked about each item again (keychain.rs). Windows' Credential Manager never asks, and limits a credential's secret to 2,560 bytes.
decision: keychain_win.rs keeps each secret as its own generic credential, Keepr/<account>, persisted on the machine, under the same account names as macOS. A share's login saved by Windows (a domain credential for the server) supplies the user name; its password can't be read by any app, so Keepr connects with the name and no password and Windows uses it.
title: Windows passwords: one Credential Manager credential per secret

consequences: A NAS that announces itself is listed; Windows PCs usually don't announce their shares, so their names are typed. Errors are Windows' WNet codes, worded as smb.rs words NetFS's. Not yet tried against a real server on Windows.
context: smb.rs mounts with NetFS, lists shares with smbutil through a pseudo-terminal and finds servers by Bonjour; none of that exists on Windows, where a share is reached by its UNC path once a connection to it exists.
decision: smb_win.rs connects with WNetAddConnection2 and no local name (\\server\share), so the share's path is its UNC path; find_mount looks through the connected resources; unmount cancels the connection Keepr made. Shares are listed with NetShareEnum after a connection to IPC$ with the login given. Servers are found with Windows' own DnsServiceBrowse for _smb._tcp.local (Windows 10 1809 and later).
title: SMB on Windows: connections without a drive letter, shares from NetShareEnum, servers by DNS-SD

consequences: On Windows the instructions count as part of the first user message rather than the system prompt. macOS is unchanged.
context: Ask's instructions carry the whole in-app guide, about 40 KB, passed on the command line as Claude Code's --append-system-prompt and Codex's developer_instructions. Windows holds a command line to 32,767 characters, and npm's .cmd shims can't pass newlines. Brainstead and Tidemark met both.
decision: On Windows (assistant/mod.rs PROMPT_ON_STDIN) Claude Code, Codex and Copilot read the message on stdin, and the instructions open a chat's first message (<instructions>...</instructions>), as Copilot's already did everywhere; a follow-up resumes the session and sends only the question. Antigravity keeps its instructions in its agent file and the question on the command line, refused past 30,000 characters. CLIs are found in their installers' folders, npm's folder or by where, an npm shim replaced by the program in its package, run with no console window and stopped with taskkill /T. The guide is filtered for the platform (<!-- mac --> and <!-- windows --> parts) as the help drawer filters it.
title: Ask on Windows: the question on stdin, the instructions in a chat's first message

consequences: A new menu item needs a place in the tray or Settings on Windows. Windows updates arrive some minutes after the Mac's. The updater's install exits the app at once on Windows, so what quitting does runs before it (updates.rs).
context: Keepr is a menu-bar app with an app menu (About, Check for Updates..., Help) and runs plan commands with zsh -lc. The sibling apps settled how each of these goes on Windows.
decision: On Windows there's no menu bar: the notification-area window adds Keepr Help (Ctrl+?) and Check for Updates..., and Settings has Check for Updates... beside Website. The tray icon is in colour (tools/make_icons.py tray-win*.png), opens on a left or right click, above a taskbar at the foot of the screen, with no shadow box. Closing the window keeps Keepr in the notification area, as on macOS. A second launch brings the running copy forward (tauri-plugin-single-instance, release builds only and not with KEEPR_DATA, so a debug build runs beside the installed app). Open at Login is the HKCU Run key with --login, honouring Startup apps' switch. Before and after commands run in PowerShell (process.rs shell). Data is in %APPDATA%\Keepr; the per-user NSIS uninstaller removes it when asked, and the Run entries always. Publishing a release starts windows-release.yml, which adds Keepr_x64-setup.exe and windows-x86_64 to latest.json (tools/update_windows.py); windows-tests.yml runs clippy and the tests on windows-latest.
title: Windows app shell: notification area, no menu bar, PowerShell for commands, releases from CI

consequences: A backup made on a Mac reads the same on a PC: its home-folder paths restore to the same folders on C:. Any new file-system call on an app path must go through paths::native, and any path given back to the page through paths::app, or it breaks only on Windows. Tests name sources with backup::tests::key.
context: Keepr is to run on Windows too, applying what the Two-edged Sword, Tidemark and Brainstead ports learned. Snapshots name each source by its absolute path, and the engine, the app and the page all split paths on '/'.
decision: As Tidemark: every path in Keepr (snapshot sources and trees, plans, the page) is written with '/', and on Windows '/' is the system drive's root (a folder on C: keeps its path after the letter, in '/' form), another drive keeps its letter (D:/Photos) and a share is //server/share. engine/src/paths.rs has native() and app(); backup::run names sources by app() and reads native(), restore writes to native(), and the page shows paths as Windows writes them (src/platform.ts shown). Leave-out rules match in any case on Windows.
title: Windows port: app paths keep macOS's form, converted only at the file system

consequences: Windows backups match the Mac's when the helper is installed. The helper is versioned (helper_win.rs VERSION): a change to its protocol means Settings offers Update, and backups fall back until then. The plan's journal id is kept in PlanState.fs_journal. Integration tests against the installed helper are ignored by default.
context: D-20261020-02 left Windows without a still copy or a change record, because Volume Shadow Copy and the NTFS change journal need an administrator. The user judged a one-time administrator prompt justified. A test on the PC showed an unelevated process can read files through a shadow copy's device path, so only making and deleting the copy, and reading the journal, need the privilege. The windows crate has no IVssBackupComponents (it isn't plain COM).
decision: Keepr Helper is a copy of Keepr.exe in Program Files run by SYSTEM as a service (--helper-service), installed or removed from Settings by running Keepr.exe --helper-install <SID> / --helper-uninstall elevated (one UAC prompt), and removed by the uninstaller's hook. It answers on \\.\pipe\keepr-helper (no remote clients; DACL: SYSTEM, administrators and the installing users' SIDs from HKLM\SOFTWARE\Keepr Helper; the client checks the server is in session 0), one JSON request per line: snapshot (Win32_ShadowCopy.Create ClientAccessible via WMI, deleted on release, when the connection closes, or at the next start from a list in ProgramData), journal (FSCTL_QUERY_USN_JOURNAL) and changes (FSCTL_READ_USN_JOURNAL since a position, parents resolved with OpenFileById, only under roots the client can open itself, untrusted past 50,000 folders or when the journal was remade). still_win.rs and fsevents_win.rs use it for sources all on one fixed NTFS drive; Keepr reads the copy as the user. Without the helper, backups are as D-20261020-02.
title: Windows still copies and the change journal through Keepr Helper, a service installed once with an administrator

consequences: A new screen needs a guide step linking to it, or the guides test fails. A sentence explaining keys in the help must not contain glyphs: shortcut() rewrites them on Windows.
context: The user wanted Keepr's help to match the sibling apps (Brainstead's cd2a3c6, Two-edged Sword's 27d255d): the drawer listed the screen's topic, then the guides, the screen's keys and topic pills at its foot, with every section open at once.
decision: Under the search box, Getting started (the list of guides, view start) and an All topics picker of every screen-kind topic; nothing follows the topic. A topic shows one section open at a time (HelpDrawer's opened state), the first by default. Keyboard shortcuts is a topic like the rest, opened at the screen's section (KEY_SECTION) and drawn as key rows; the topic pills and the keys block are gone. Ten guides cover every screen (a test checks each screen but Search is reached by one). src/help/GuideOffer.tsx offers Getting started when the window opens, once a launch and not in screenshot mode, until Don't ask me again or Settings' Offer Getting started when Keepr opens (settings.offerGuide) turns it off.
title: Help drawer: Getting started and an All topics picker at the top, one section open, keys a topic of their own, offered at startup
